Container.Name: github-runner
Container.Overview: Self-hosted GitHub Actions runner. Minutes on a self-hosted runner do not count against the account's Actions allowance, which is the point of running one: a repository whose CI runs a full test suite against a real database service container is what consumes that allowance. ONE neutral template for the whole fleet — nothing here is specific to a repository or a host. At creation set: ACCESS_TOKEN (a fine-grained PAT with Administration: read+write on the target repo), REPO_URL, RUNNER_NAME, and LABELS. Each instance registers itself on start and appears under the repository's Settings -> Actions -> Runners; a workflow targets it with runs-on: [self-hosted, <one of your LABELS>]. NETWORK MODE IS LOAD-BEARING, see the note on the Docker socket below — the default of host is deliberate, and a bridge runner cannot reach service containers. One runner executes ONE job at a time; add a second instance (a different Name and RUNNER_NAME) for concurrency.
Container.Description: Self-hosted GitHub Actions runner (neutral template). Set the PAT, the repository URL, a runner name and labels at creation; mount the Docker socket so workflow jobs can build images and start service containers.

Config.Name: Docker socket
Config.Description: REQUIRED for any workflow that builds an image or declares a services: container. Grants this container control of the host's Docker daemon, which is effectively host root — run this only for repositories whose workflow code you trust, since a workflow can run anything the socket allows. Remove it only if every workflow you run is pure script.

Config.Name: ACCESS_TOKEN
Config.Description: GitHub Personal Access Token, used ONCE PER START to obtain a short-lived runner registration token. Fine-grained, scoped to the target repository only, with Administration: read and write. It is not the runner's identity — the runner authenticates with its own credential after registering — so this token can be rotated without disturbing an already-registered runner until its next restart.

Config.Name: REPO_URL
Config.Description: Full URL of the repository this runner serves, e.g. https://github.com/<owner>/<repo> . Must match the scope below: a repo-scoped runner needs a repository URL, an org-scoped one needs the organisation URL.

Config.Name: RUNNER_NAME
Config.Description: The name this runner registers under, e.g. <runner-name>. It is shown in the repository's runner list AND in the job log of every workflow run — on a PUBLIC repository those logs are world-readable, so choose a name that reveals nothing about the machine (prefer <repo>-runner-1 over anything naming the host). Must be unique within the scope; a second instance needs a different one.

Config.Name: RUNNER_SCOPE
Config.Description: What REPO_URL points at: repo (a single repository) or org (every repository in an organisation). Leave at repo unless you deliberately want one runner serving many repositories — an org runner accepts jobs from any of them, so it is only as trustworthy as the least trustworthy workflow in the org.

Config.Name: LABELS
Config.Description: Comma-separated labels a workflow selects this runner by, e.g. self-hosted or self-hosted,<repo>. `self-hosted`, `Linux` and `X64` are applied automatically and cannot be removed, so a bare runs-on: self-hosted already reaches every runner you own — give each runner ONE distinguishing label and target runs-on: [self-hosted, <that label>] once you have more than one. Same caution as RUNNER_NAME: labels appear in public workflow logs, so keep them neutral.

Config.Name: RUNNER_WORKDIR
Config.Description: Where the runner checks code out INSIDE this container. Leave as-is unless you are also setting the optional Work Directory mount below, in which case the two must agree.

Config.Name: Work directory (optional)
Config.Description: OPTIONAL and normally left EMPTY. Set it only to run jobs in a job container (the workflow `container:` key), and then the host path MUST be identical to the container path, with RUNNER_WORKDIR inside it — host /tmp/runner, container /tmp/runner, RUNNER_WORKDIR /tmp/runner/work. A mismatch does not error; the job container silently mounts an empty workspace.

Config.Name: EPHEMERAL
Config.Description: OPTIONAL. Set to true to make the runner accept exactly ONE job and then deregister, so nothing survives from one job to the next. That is the safer posture for anything running untrusted code, but it needs a restart policy that brings the container back after each job, or the runner simply disappears after one. Leave blank for a persistent runner.

Config.Name: RUNNER_GROUP
Config.Description: OPTIONAL. Runner group to register into; blank uses Default. Only meaningful for org-scoped runners.
